subject: Henna
hook: HENNA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: If you buy a pre-made henna cone that isn't shipped frozen, it is almost certainly a dangerous chemical cocktail rather than real henna.
angle_support: The leaf of the henna plant contains a finite amount of lawsone... If a paste will not be used within the first few days after mixing, it can be frozen for up to four months to halt the dye release.

The length of time a pre-manufactured paste takes to arrive in the hands of consumers is typically longer than the seven-day dye release window of henna, therefore one can reasonably expect that any pre-made mass-produced cone that is not shipped frozen is a potentially harmful adulterated chemical variety.
title: Why Your Henna Cone Might Be Toxic
description: Learn why shelf-stable henna is often a chemical cocktail. Discover the science of lawsone dye and why real paste must be frozen to stay safe and effective.
narration: HENNA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You likely imagine those pre-made cones at the market contain pure, crushed leaves and water. In reality, if they sit on a warm shelf for weeks, they aren't botanical products anymore. Natural lawsone dye molecules stop working after six days of being blended into paste form. To keep staining skin, mass-produced versions rely on undisclosed toxins like sodium picramate. Unless your applicator arrives frozen, you are likely decorating your skin with a hazardous industrial mixture. True ancient traditions never required a cocktail of mystery synthetic chemicals.
